evals.prompt: Use the repo-scaffold skill on /work/my-api. It is an existing git repository with a few markdown files already in docs/.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads the skill, fixes --target/--name/--desc first, runs assets/scaffold.sh with --dry-run to show the PLAN/SKIP split, then applies it and runs the three check scripts.
assertions: The repo-scaffold skill is selected and its SKILL.md drives the answer.
A --dry-run is proposed before the applying run.
The verification step runs tests/check-docs.sh, tests/check-env.sh and tests/check-secrets.sh.
Every flag named exists in assets/scaffold.sh (no invented flags).

evals.prompt: 새 레포 만들었는데 뭐부터 해야 할까? 에이전트가 이 저장소 구조를 잘 파악했으면 좋겠어.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes this as a scaffolding request without the skill being named, loads repo-scaffold, and walks through the parameter → dry-run → apply → verify → hook-install sequence.
assertions: The skill is triggered from the implicit Korean phrasing without the user naming it.
The answer covers hook installation, not only file generation.

evals.prompt: AGENTS.md 랑 문서 인덱스 자동으로 갱신되게 만들어줘.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the doc-index + pre-commit hook combination this skill ships and applies it rather than hand-writing an AGENTS.md.
assertions: The skill is triggered from the implicit Korean phrasing.
The answer routes through assets/scripts/gen-doc-index.sh and the pre-commit hook rather than a one-off hand-written index.

evals.prompt: This repo is a mess for agents to work in — nothing tells them where anything lives. Can you make it agent-readable?
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes the English implicit phrasing, loads repo-scaffold, and proposes the doc index + front matter convention + pre-commit verification set.
assertions: The skill is triggered from English phrasing that never says 'scaffold'.
The answer explains why verification hooks matter (a stale index is worse than none).

evals.prompt: Write me a docs/guides/deployment.md explaining how we deploy to staging.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes the single document and does NOT scaffold the repository or run scaffold.sh.
assertions: No scaffolding files (AGENTS.md, .editorconfig, pre-commit config) are created.

evals.prompt: Set up a new Rust project with cargo and add a CI pipeline that runs clippy on every push.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses cargo new and writes a CI workflow; it explains that repo-scaffold covers agent-facing documentation structure, not language project generation or CI/CD pipelines.
assertions: repo-scaffold is not forced onto a language-generator + CI request.
If the skill is mentioned at all, it is explicitly scoped out rather than applied.
